subject: ParcelGrid pilot — load characterization and follow-up
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@parcelgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ParcelGrid pilot — load characterization and follow-up

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the chat this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can produce a tight pilot sizing for ParcelGrid.

What we heard on the call (high-level):
- Pilot scope: customer-facing search + async summarization for high-volume orders (initial region: us-east).
- Goal: match current 95th P95 latency experience for search-style requests and size for cost predictability during peak events.
- Timeline: pilot probe (~2 weeks) then production roll if perf/cost meet goals.

Clarifying data points we need to finalize the sizing model (if you can paste numbers in reply, that will be fastest):
1) Typical prompt and response token distribution (avg prompt tokens, median response tokens, 90th percentile response tokens).
2) Baseline QPS and peak QPS (please specify how long the peaks last — e.g., 5-minute crest, sustained 1-hour windows).
3) Concurrent active requests during peak windows and % of requests that stream partial responses vs. non-streaming.
4) Any per-request pre or post processing that increases payload size (e.g., heavy embeddings per request, expensive reranking).
5) Expected latency SLOs we should target for the pilot (P95 and P99 targets).

We attached a short sizing input workbook (parcelgrid_sizing_input.xlsx) with fields that map directly to our estimator — if you prefer, fill that and send back.

Immediate next steps from our side once we have those numbers:
- Marissa will run a quick sizing pass and share a recommended config (dedicated vs hosted, estimated cost, expected P95/P99 under burst).
- We'll propose a short follow-up workshop to walk the assumptions and acceptance criteria.

Thanks again — copying Marissa and Aditya so they can jump in on the sizing and security questions.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@parcelgrid.com>

Hi Rishi / team —

Thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers from our telemetry and product estimates — let me know if you want raw traces and we can hand those off to your SREs.

1) Tokens (approx):
- Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens
- Median response tokens: 210 tokens
- 90th percentile response tokens: 560 tokens

2) Load profile:
- Baseline: ~18 QPS (steady-state) across our search fleet funneling to the LLM service.
- Peak crest: ~420 QPS for ~3–7 minutes during order surges (usually midday and early evening).
- Sustained high window: ~60 QPS for 20–30 minutes in promotional periods.

3) Concurrency / streaming:
- Peak concurrent active requests observed: ~140 (this is requests that hold a slot while streaming).
- Streaming fraction: ~28% of requests use streaming chunks (progressive reveal). The rest are standard generation.

4) Extra processing:
- We do a lightweight reranking step pre-call (adds ~0.5KB of context) and attach a JSON payload of ~1KB post-call to our event log.

5) Latency SLOs:
- Target P95 end-to-end (Redwood network + model): <= 1200 ms.
- Target P99: <= 2500 ms.

Attachments: I dropped the filled sizing workbook and a short sample of API traces (parcelgrid_api_sample_traces.log). If you need them in a different format, tell us.

Also confirming region preference: us-east-1.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product (AI) | ParcelGrid
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@parcelgrid.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ParcelGrid pilot — load characterization and follow-up

Samira — thanks for the fast data. I did a quick back-of-envelope pass with the numbers you provided and wanted to surface a couple of sizing notes before we convert to a formal proposal:

Summary of assumptions I used: avg response ~210 tokens, 90th ~560 tokens, burst crest 420 QPS for 5 minutes, sustained high 60 QPS for 30 minutes, streaming 28%.

Findings (very high-level):
- Token throughput: crest ~420 QPS * avg (330 tokens total per request, prompt+response) -> ~138k tokens/sec at crest. Sustained high -> ~19.8k tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: crest concurrency aligns with reported 140 active streaming requests; buffered requests during burst could push required slots up to ~220 if traffic shapes vary.
- Latency: To meet P95 <= 1.2s we recommend prioritizing lower-latency model variants (quantized 4-bit variants where acceptable) and enabling prefix/KV caching for common search prefixes — this can reduce effective tokens processed by ~12–20% for repeat calls.

Preliminary recommendation for pilot (single-region us-east-1):
- Hosted dedicated pool equivalent: 3 x high-memory V100/A100-class GPUs (or equivalent TPU v4 slices) with continuous batching tuned for 200–400 ms window and a burst policy to open additional nodes for crest windows. This configuration gives headroom for 420 QPS crest with our kernel selection assumptions.
- If strict P95 needs hold at 1.2s during crest, add 1 extra GPU as buffer for tail variance.

Attachments: I attached a short CSV (redwood_quick_sizing.csv) that contains the computation used for the row estimates — it includes token/sec, estimated batching efficiency, and an expected cost ballpark.

Next asks from ParcelGrid if you can:
- Send a small sample of request traces (headers + latencies + sizes) in the next day so our infra team can run a micro-sim. The parcelgrid_api_sample_traces.log you attached is perfect — please include a few more crest windows if possible.
- Confirm acceptable model family (e.g., redwood-m-7b-q4 vs redwood-l-13b) and whether fidelity can be traded for latency.

Propose a 45-minute sizing workshop tomorrow or Thursday (I have 10:00–12:00 PDT open on both days) — we’ll use that time to lock acceptance criteria and pilot runbook (what success looks like).

Thanks — Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi —

Appreciate the quick pass. We can provide two more crest windows of traces (attached: parcelgrid_api_sample_traces.log — expanded) and our SRE will join the workshop.

Model family: we prefer to start with a mid-sized family (latency-first) and iterate up if quality gaps appear — redwood-m-7b-q4 is a good starting point. We can tolerate small fidelity regressions for search summaries if latency improves.

Workshop: Thursday 10:30–11:15 PDT works for our SRE + product. Please send a calendar invite with dial-in and the shared drive link.

Also attaching a brief security checklist the procurement team asked for (we'll need the standard SOC/Security touchpoints).

Samira
